sentences.text: Researchers investigated whether inhibiting the FLT3 kinase could boost KCC2, a transporter that helps neurons maintain inhibitory signals, using a functional genomics approach on neurons from mice and human stem cells. A genetic screen with CRISPR technology further revealed that FLT3 controls specific gene networks involved in DNA packaging and brain inflammation.

In mice treated with kainic acid, the drug KW-2449 crossed into the brain, raised KCC2 levels for up to 24 hours, and lowered seizure occurrence. The authors conclude these results show FLT3 has a new role in brain function and provide initial proof that blocking it could lead to new anti-seizure drugs, though more development is needed.
